ConnectionStrings._comment: Local development points at EmployeeLifecycleDev, NOT the production EmployeeLifecycle database. Before this file existed, dev and prod shared one database, which meant `dotnet ef database update` from any machine was a production schema change — see CONTRIBUTING.md. EmployeeLifecycleDev is on the same vm-trm-sql1 instance with the same French_CI_AS collation as prod (collation mismatches produce subtle string-comparison and sorting differences that only show up in production). WorkdayDb still points at the real Redingote because it is read-only and externally managed — there is nothing to protect it from.
